answer: In an AI agent economy, every agent must lock collateral to act, so a Sybil attacker pays real cost per fake identity. An honest agent weaves one identity thread through a shared reputation ledger; each newcomer stakes first, then earns trust by finishing verifiable tasks. The orchard of verified peers grows only when staked agents vouch for newcomers, and a low-reputation account never gains a haven of full privileges. Spawning thousands of sock-puppets multiplies locked funds and slashing risk, while consensus ignores identities whose collateral cannot cover the harm they could cause.
